note.question: How does a trade agent shape newsvendor model?
note.overview: This paper studies the procurement decisions of a trade agent: The agent chooses a bid (unit price to pay) to procure the goods available from seller(s). If the agent wins the bid, the supply is used to meet the buyer’s demand. The trade agent’s single-period, single-product problem is a new type of newsvendor problem.

source.section: Goods for a Trade Agent Procuring Supplies
source.quote: When a seller’s mean yield increases and all other parameters remain the same, the agent’s optimal bid may increase or decrease depend­ ing on the demand-to-supply ratio which can be used as a measure of scarcity.

In addition to the uncertainty in the bid outcome, we incorporate the traditional yield uncertainty to the problem: Although the quantity available for sale is known for each seller, there is no guarantee that the entire lot will be available on time or in good condition to meet the demand.
The yield model here is no different from the classical yield uncer­ tainty models in the supply chain literature.
